newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank says no intervention on rates.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank says no intervention on rates.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Sunday the bank would not interfere with local banks' decision to lower interest rates.
"Every bank is free to set its deposit and lending rates," Sheu said on state-funded television. He was commenting on Saturday's decision by two state banks to further ease their interest rates.
"The central bank will not intervene," Sheu said.

Two of Taiwan's Big Three state banks -- Hua Nan Bank and First Commercial Bank -- announced their second rate cuts in one month, cutting their prime lending rate by 0.025 percentage points to 7.525 percent from 7.550, effective on Monday.
Other major banks are expected to follow suit and cut their rates, state television said.
Despite the central bank maintaining an "appropriately loose" monetary policy, the island's economy remains slugglish.
The central bank board decided on Saturday to leave Taiwan's monetary policy unchanged and set a November 14 meeting to further review the island's reserve system.
